messages:
julia_customer: Hey team — hitting a 400 when using function calls to the `lookup_user` tool. Started after a small change on our side. Error payload attached. Anyone seen this?

sarah_support: sorry you're blocked, julia. can you paste minimal curl + body you used?

julia_customer: sure — here's the exact request we send from our backend (node):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-***' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  \"model\": \"rwd-open-1\",
  \"input\": \"Find user\",
  \"function_call\": {\"name\":\"lookup_user\"},
  \"tool_call\": {
    \"name\": \"lookup_user\",
    \"arguments\": \"{\\\"user_id\\\": \\\"u-123\\\", \\\"debug\\\": true}\"
  }
}'

julia_customer: response: 
{
  \"error\": \"tool_call.arguments validation failed\",
  \"details\": [
    {\"path\":\"tool_call.arguments\", \"message\":\"expected object, got string\"},
    {\"path\":\"tool_call.arguments.user_id\", \"message\":\"is required\"},
    {\"path\":\"tool_call.arguments.debug\", \"message\":\"additional property not allowed\"}
  ]
}

alex_eng: ah ok — looks like the client is passing arguments as a JSON-encoded string rather than an object. our schema for tools expects a JSON object for arguments (type: object, required: [\"user_id\"]). additionalProperties is false on that schema so any extra props cause failure.

sarah_support: julia — is there any reason your code stringifies the arguments instead of passing them as an object?

julia_customer: legacy serializer on our side — we pass something like JSON.stringify(args) into the call. we didn't change the shape otherwise. it used to work for us though; not sure when it broke.

mike_sre: couple possibilities: 1) the API used to leniently coerce stringified args into objects in the runtime previously; 2) a recent validation tightening rolled out and now rejects strings. i'm going to check deploy history. pinging deploy-bot for the last infra rollout.

deploy-bot: @mike_sre Release: inference-runtime v3.17.2 deployed 2025-11-18T09:12:02Z — includes stricter JSON schema validation for tool args.

mike_sre: confirmed — rollout included stricter validation (reject string args). this matches julia's timing.

alex_eng: from an engineering POV we consider stringified args a client bug — function/tool calling relies on machine-readable objects. however we should give a clear error message and a migration-friendly guidance. current error mixes three validation messages which is not great.

sarah_support: julia, quick workaround: stop stringifying tool args. set tool_call.arguments to a JSON object, e.g.:

\"tool_call\": {
  \"name\": \"lookup_user\",
  \"arguments\": {\"user_id\": \"u-123\"}
}

julia_customer: ok will try now. also what's the recommended handling for small debug fields? we sometimes attach transient debug flags in prod.

alex_eng: for now remove debug from the args schema (server disallows additionalProperties). if you need ad-hoc metadata, add a top-level metadata field that the tool schema explicitly accepts, or update your tool definition to allow that property. we can also relax the schema on our side but prefer explicitness.

julia_customer: updated request, sending...

julia_customer: works now — 200 and tool returned user payload. thanks.

sarah_support: great! i'll keep the thread open while we discuss longer-term improvements with eng.

alex_eng: short-term action items: 1) make error messages clearer (map validation errors to human-friendly text), 2) add a dedicated note in docs/quickstart about not stringifying tool args, 3) consider an opt-in leniency flag for enterprise customers who rely on the old behavior.

mike_sre: ops item: add rollout note to changelog to call out schema tightening. this caused a customer-impact incident.

sarah_support: cc product for docs update — @alex_eng can you open a small PR for docs?

alex_eng: opened docs PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/docs/pulls/542 — adds example and explanation.

alex_eng: also sending a small runtime patch idea: if tool_call.arguments is a string, attempt JSON.parse; if parse succeeds and result is an object, accept but log a warning at warn level and emit a deprecation notice for one month. if parse fails or result isn't object, keep rejecting. thoughts?

mike_sre: compromise seems reasonable to reduce customer scatter. we'd need telemetry for how many incoming requests relied on this behavior. can you add a feature flag behind which this parsing runs?

alex_eng: yep - feature-flagged. i'll make it off by default and enable for a week in staging.

sarah_support: julia — do you want us to enable the leniency flag for your org while you fix code? we can do a short window.

julia_customer: that would be amazing. a 24-hour window to patch will be enough.

mike_sre: enabling leniency for org: org-julia-corp for 24h. feature-flag id: ff-tool-args-coerce — enabled until 2025-11-25T15:10:00Z.

deploy-bot: Feature flag ff-tool-args-coerce enabled for org-julia-corp by mike_sre at 2025-11-24T14:58:12Z.

julia_customer: verified we can keep old behavior and will push fix in next deploy. thanks everyone.

sarah_support: marking this as tracked issue SUP-1321. we'll follow up when docs PR merges and runtime patch is staged.

alex_eng: follow-up: changed error payload to be more explicit (will land in v3.17.3):

OLD: {\"error\":\"tool_call.arguments validation failed\", \"details\": [...] }
NEW: {\"error\":\"invalid_tool_arguments\", \"message\":\"tool 'lookup_user' expected an object for 'arguments' but received a string. try passing arguments as a JSON object (not a string). For migration we can temporarily accept stringified JSON if feature flag enabled.\", \"hint\":\"remove JSON.stringify on the client or enable ff-tool-args-coerce for a short window.\"}

sarah_support: julia — after your org finishes patching we'll disable the leniency flag and close SUP-1321. feel free to reopen if anything else. :thumbsup:

julia_customer: will do. appreciate the quick turnaround and the deprecation path.

mike_sre: logging note: added a saved search in Splunk to find 'invalid_tool_arguments' and requests where tool_call.arguments is a string to help product prioritize.

sarah_support: closing thread for now. reopen if there are regressions.
